acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Mummies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Sacred Servant, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Processional Glyph Scribe (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A fully wrapped ritual attendant with gilded bands layered over linen, a jeweled pectoral collar with an opening front clasp, and three long glyph-inscribed strips controlled by stiff fingers.

Signature mechanic: Written Procession: the Servant extends three gilded bands from its jeweled collar, touching floor points in a clearly numbered glyph order. After the third point, the bands tighten in reverse and drag anyone standing on a recorded segment back toward the previous point. Crossing two bands before completion tangles them; striking the open collar clasp cancels the rewind.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter into ordered route control by unspooling three gilded glyph bands that record movement and then rewind along the same processional sequence.
constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity materials remain dry linen, desiccated flesh, bronze, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, turquoise, sandstone grave goods, burial dust, and ordinary tomb sand with visible age and craft.

Motion and effects stay funerary and mechanical: bandages tighten, knots turn, charms strike linen, glyph ink conducts faint ritual light, dust shakes from folds, and sand moves only when a wrapped foot, mask, weapon, or sarcophagus displaces it.
counterplay: Track the numbered glow, leave the latest segment, cross two loose bands to tangle them, or strike the exposed collar clasp before the hands complete their cross. Affinity signal: Loose end knots, bronze stitches, interrupted glyphs, mask straps, cartouche seals, sarcophagus hinges, and exposed dried flesh preserve every established weak point.
forbiddenTreatments: Treating family-native sand, dust, sandstone, faint glyph light, or gold alone as an elemental affinity
identityInvariants: A stiff-limbed human or humanoid silhouette remains wrapped from head to foot, with arms held forward, crossed, guarding, inscribing, or commanding through readable linen tension.
Sun-bleached linen, sand beige, desert ochre, deep gold, lapis blue, and turquoise remain funerary materials and symbols rather than affinity colors.
Linen bandage, dried flesh, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, bronze, and sandstone grave goods stay materially distinct and retain visible knots, stitches, glyph routes, and breakable seals.
Family-native sand and dust follow disturbed wrappings, tomb movement, and burial objects without becoming Earth or Wind affinity by themselves.
Escalation adds precious thread, glyph density, collars, masks, armor, headdresses, and sarcophagus regalia while the bandages never come off and always explain binding and counterplay.
telegraph: The jeweled collar opens at one front clasp, faint family-native glyph light travels one-two-three along separate bands, and the Servant's stiff hands cross before the order reverses.
